title: A 6.78MHz Single-Stage Regulating Rectifier with Dual Outputs Simultaneously Charged in a Half Cycle Achieving 92.2% Efficiency and 131mW Output Power
problem: Wireless power transfer (WPT) to implanted biomedical devices requires efficient power conditioning, and implants often need multiple output voltages (e.g., low voltage for biopotential recording, high voltage for neurostimulation) with different performance requirements (stability vs. bandwidth). Single-output rectifiers cannot simultaneously meet these conflicting demands.
motivation: Implanted biomedical devices eliminate battery-replacement burden and enable new form factors, but multi-voltage on-chip power delivery increases complexity—efficient, fully-integrated multi-output rectifiers enable more functional implant designs.
method: Single-stage regulating rectifier with dual simultaneous outputs per half-cycle at 6.78MHz switching frequency. The architecture achieves independent regulation of two output voltages: low stable voltage (V_OUT2) for recording front-end and high-bandwidth voltage (V_OUT1) for stimulation back-end, within a single rectifier stage rather than cascading multiple stages.
key_novelty: Single-stage rectifier topology enabling simultaneous dual-output charging and independent regulation in a half-cycle to meet conflicting voltage/bandwidth requirements of implant power delivery.
contributions: Single-stage dual-output regulating rectifier eliminating need for multiple cascaded power stages
92.2% power efficiency with 131mW output power capability
Independent regulation of low-voltage recording output (stable, low noise) and high-voltage stimulation output (high bandwidth, high current)
6.78MHz switching enables compact on-chip integration for implanted devices
baselines: Separate recording and stimulation power supplies
limitations: Not discussed—load-regulation range, PSRR, output ripple specifications not specified in abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient single-stage dual-output rectifier for implanted biomedical devices
